title: Lack of adequate computers delayed discovery of complexity from simple rules

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Lack of adequate computers delayed discovery of complexity from simple rules

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A main reason that complexity from simple programs was not discovered before the 1980s is that computer technology powerful enough for the required large-scale exploratory experiments did not yet exist, together with a lack of intuition drawn from practical computing.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: one of the main reasons that the discoveries I describe in this chapter were not made before the 1980s is just that computer technology did not yet exist powerful enough to do the kinds of exploratory experiments that were needed.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 2, “The Crucial Experiment”; section “Why These Discoveries Were Not Made Before” (from p. 42), p. 46. Scope: history of science and computing

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch02-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Historical hardware and literature records can test feasibility and chronology. They cannot cleanly quantify the relative causal importance of computing power versus conceptual and social factors.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct pre-1980 computing capabilities, published explorations, and researchers' stated constraints, then estimate whether the relevant enumerations and visualizations were technically feasible. Compare the technology account with institutional, conceptual, and priority-based alternatives.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Main reason is a counterfactual causal attribution.

Publication records incompletely capture unpublished exploration and intuition.

Small earlier computations may have sufficed for some discoveries.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Museum catalogs and digitized technical literature can establish when graphics-capable machines made large rule surveys cheap. That tests the technological timeline. The claim that this absence was a main reason the phenomenon stayed unseen is confounded with the conceptual factors the same passage mentions, and those factors are not separated by the hardware record.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Date the availability of interactive computers able to display large cellular-automaton surveys, and compare that date with the late-1970s and 1980s explorations. The chronology can support or weaken the technology clause. It cannot by itself show that missing computers were a main reason, as opposed to missing motivation to look.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Some relevant machines and manual explorations predate the 1980s, so the cutoff is graded.

A main reason is a causal claim confounded with the lack of a reason to run the experiments.
